key_concept: Electrode potentials are intensive and cannot be added or subtracted directly; combine half-reactions through $\Delta G^\circ = -nFE^\circ$, which is additive.
steps: Write the given couples: (i) $Fe^{3+} + 3e^- \rightarrow Fe$, $E_1^\circ = -0.04$ V, $n_1 = 3$; (ii) $Fe^{2+} + 2e^- \rightarrow Fe$, $E_2^\circ = -0.44$ V, $n_2 = 2$.
why_not_others: $+0.40$ V comes from directly subtracting potentials, $(-0.04) - (-0.44)$, while ignoring the number of electrons. $-0.48$ V comes from simply adding the potentials, and $+0.92$ V comes from mixing up the electron-weighting terms. None of these accounts correctly for $nE^\circ$.
common_trap: Students subtract the two $E^\circ$ values directly and get $+0.40$ V, forgetting that only $nE^\circ$ (i.e. $\Delta G^\circ$) is additive.
time_saving_tip: Use $n_3E_3^\circ = n_1E_1^\circ - n_2E_2^\circ$ directly: $1 \cdot E^\circ = 3(-0.04) - 2(-0.44) = 0.76$ V.
